hints: Start by sorting the four types: who makes the antibodies, you or someone else? Remember active means you make them, passive means you receive them.
Now think about memory cells versus donated antibodies. Which one gives long term protection and which one is quickly broken down?
walkthrough:
**Sort Active Versus Passive**

Great first move is to get the definitions straight. Active immunity means your own B-lymphocytes make antibodies and make memory cells. Passive immunity means you are given ready made antibodies from elsewhere, so you make no memory cells.

Natural just means infection or mother to baby. Artificial just means medical intervention like a vaccine or an antibody injection.

**Compare How Long They Last**

This is the key idea for this question. Active immunity is long lasting because memory B and T cells stay for years, often for life. Passive immunity is short lived because donated antibodies are proteins that are broken down in weeks to months and are not replaced.

**Apply To The Options**

Artificial active (vaccination) gives you memory cells, so it lasts years. Natural passive (antibodies across the placenta or in breast milk) gives only temporary antibodies, so it lasts weeks to months. That makes artificial active much longer lasting, so B is correct.

options.A: Artificial active immunity is vaccination, you produce your own antibodies, there is no donation. Only passive immunity involves donation.
options.B: Correct. Artificial active immunity creates memory cells and lasts years, while natural passive antibodies are broken down in weeks to months.
options.C: Both are active immunity, so both involve a slow primary response then a fast secondary response on re-exposure. One is not inherently faster than the other.
options.D: Specific B-lymphocyte recognition and binding happens in all active immunity, both natural (infection) and artificial (vaccine), not only in natural immunity.
